title: Two Crossing Stars
mood: Two lights climb toward the chest of something vast, crossing and crossing again like fireworks.

hero.alt: Guinevere and Vexana stand side by side under a storm sky, her two drones up with their red fists and the staff glowing in Vexana's hand; then a vast dark winged shape spreads over the ruined city, two small figures facing it below.

segs.t: Guinevere climbed with the wind in her face and Vexana beside her.
Her wings were thin, but they held. Both drones rode at her shoulders, still trailing smoke. Below, the platform shrank to a slab of black glass, with four small figures on it under a glow of pink.
Ahead, the Mother Matrix took up half the sky. White light was gathering in its chest.
She looked at the staff in Vexana’s right hand. The orb was dark again.
At the end of their fight over the gap, she had flown at Vexana with everything she had left. Then white, and falling.
At the last meter, something had gone past her ear, close enough to hear it hum.
The staff.
She had felt it go by and shoved it down. There had been no time. Now she let herself look at it.
She missed,
thought Guinevere.
Vexana never misses. She turned it aside, with every Ender watching.
Vexana’s hair streamed back, blue-lavender running into magenta. Her burned arm was tucked against her ribs.
Guinevere called to her across the wind. “Vexana... to the future where you are.”
“This is the final farewell,” said Vexana.
She meant it.

The Matrix hung right in front of the Singularity, its chest before the middle of the star. The star’s torn edges were bright. Its middle had no light at all. From where they climbed, a small black point showed there beside the chest, and the clouds bent around it as the wind dragged them in.

media.alt: A dark winged shape hangs in front of a vast four-pointed tear of violet light above the ruined city, the tear's edges burning bright.

segs.t: Vexana knew what it was. On the prow of the Storm Citadel, Obsidia had told her. A door held open this wide and this long grew a drain at its center, a black hole. It reached only a short way, and it took only what had no strength left to hold against it. Whatever crossed the middle, it unmade.
“Nothing made of matter ever comes back out,” Obsidia had said.
The chest sat in front of that drain. To strike it, they would have to fly inside its reach. After the strike, there would be nothing left in them to hold against it.
Once, alone in the Academy library, she had asked for anything on the void. The third paper had Teacher Chang’e’s name on it.
Status: untested.
It said an Aspirant’s light would go on shining inside a black hole, and find its way home.
Vexana did not know if it was true. Nobody did.
On the platform she had told Guinevere to go, and then taken her hand. She would not tell her to go again.
“Plan A first,” said Guinevere.

On the green-railed roof, the day Vexana told her about the paper, Guinevere had laid it out. “Plan A, I smash the Core and we win. Plan B, we come home.” Then she had made Vexana say “Plan B” out loud. When the siren went, she had hauled her up by the hand. “Plan A first.”
She had never found the Core. Obsidia had never even seen it. The open chest was the one blow left to them.
“This is Plan A,” said Vexana.
Guinevere waited for the rest. Vexana did not give it to her.
“It opens when it fires,” she said instead. “Only then.”
It had fired three times today, and she had been in front of it every time. For weeks before that she had watched its body in the dark, waiting for this.
Enders came off the Matrix’s wings.
They peeled away by the dozen and dropped at the two of them out of the gray.
Vexana’s back came against Guinevere’s. Guinevere felt her shoulder blades through the torn robe, and the staff humming behind her head.

Neither of them said left or right. A claw came at Guinevere’s blind side, and a violet shot took it before she turned. She put her fist through the open chest of the one in front. Her drones took the ones that came high.
Something dived at Vexana’s blind side. This time it was Guinevere’s fist that met it.
Like every fight that year,
she thought.
Like we never stopped.
Then the sky moved.

A hand bigger than the platform came across it, violet plate and claws. Its wind hit first. They broke apart, one up and one down, and the hand went through the place where they had been. Then they found each other again, back to back.
They went higher, around the wing, in toward the chest, to be close when it opened.
Near the middle of the star, something took hold of Guinevere’s wings. It was stronger than the wind, and it pulled one way only, in toward the black point. Her wings bent with it.
Vexana’s burned hand closed on her wrist and hauled her back.
“Not the center,” said Vexana. “Not yet.”
Guinevere looked at the black point. Light ran into it, and she saw none come out.
Final farewell,
she thought.
That’s what she meant.
And she didn’t say Plan B.
Down on the platform, Layla had the cannon on her shoulder and her cheek on the stock.
Ruby held the rail. Enders kept coming over it, and the scythe kept sending them back. Angela’s shield stood over the four of them, pink and bright.
High above, two lights wove through the gray around the Matrix’s wing, one gold and one violet. They never got in each other’s way.
“Those two are undefeated,” Professor Joe had said once, his cane pointed at their billboard. “Ask them why. They can’t tell you either.”
Layla watched them now. She still could not have told him why.
Guinevere’s line was open. Layla had heard every word of it.
This is the final farewell.
“Not on my count,” she muttered.
Chang’e came on the command channel, small and exact. “I have its signature. When it fires, the core shows three hundred meters under the crown, a little left of center.”
Weak spot,
thought Layla.
When it attacks. Obviously.
She had said it in Joe’s class as if it were easy.

She counted angles. The wind off the bay, from the left. The rail under her elbow for a rest. Once she had counted sixteen kills in one fight and been proud of it. Now she was counting for a girl she had called a traitor.
“We don’t aim at the chest,” she said. “That’s theirs. We make it look at us. Then it fires down at the shield, away from them, and the chest opens.”
“Fanny, thirty degrees up, left of the crown. Ruby, hold the rail. Angela, keep the shield high and open me a lane. On three.”
“Understood,” said Fanny.
“Ready!” said Angela.

media.alt: Four faces side by side, the team on the platform, every one of them shouting, ready.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama

segs.t: Chang’e’s voice came back. “It’s nearly full. Eight seconds.”
Layla keyed the channel. “Guinevere. When it looks at us, it’s yours.”
“One. Two.”
“Fire!” said Layla.
Angela opened one pane. Layla’s shot went up through it first, a thin cyan line, and Fanny’s arcs went after it. The pane shut. Every streak met on the crowned head and burst.
The violet eyes swung down to the platform. An arm rose toward it. Under the crown, the chest plates split.
“Now,” said Layla, to nobody.
The plates came apart, and Guinevere saw the magenta core blazing in the gap.
She went. Vexana went with her.
They dived in under the raised arm. Their two lights crossed, and crossed again, a gold star and a violet one.

media.alt: Streaks of cyan, gold and red light from below meet on the crowned head of a vast winged shape; then a red-gold light and a violet one sweep in from both sides and cross as they dive at it.
media.credit: Official Guinevere and Vexana interactive drama and Re:Link animation

segs.t: Under the fireworks at the dome’s edge, with Vexana’s hand in hers, she had pointed at the sky.
We’ll be just like fireworks, shining at our absolute brightest!
Brightest, then,
she thought.
The core came up at them, filling everything.
“This strike is for Vexana,” said Guinevere.
Beside her, in the same breath, Vexana’s voice rang out. “This strike is for Guinevere!”
They struck the open chest together, her fist beside Vexana’s staff.
Light broke out of the wound. The roar came after it and shook her teeth. The shot that had been gathering never left.
The Mother Matrix staggered. It reeled back into the light at the star’s edge with its wings flung wide, and its chest plates ground shut over the wound.
It’s going back,
thought Guinevere.
We stopped it.
Vexana had nothing left.
Her wings were threads of violet. She could not have lifted the staff again. The strike had taken all of it, as she had known it would.
The Matrix had gone back into the light. Where its chest had been, there was only the black point. They were inside its reach.
It took hold of her. She did not fight it. There was nothing to fight with.
A little way off, Guinevere was going the same way. Her light had thinned to a faint gold outline. Her face was turned toward Vexana, and she was grinning, wet-eyed, the way she had on the platform.
Nothing made of matter ever comes back out.
And her own words, on the roof.
The paper never says two. But I think two would shine brighter.
Under her sleeve the star was still warm against her wrist. She could see the other one lit at Guinevere’s collar.
“Plan B,” said Vexana.
This time nobody had asked her.
Guinevere’s light flared up gold.
It was the last thing Vexana saw.
Then the dark took them both.
